lens: Words on screen and their evidence: structural-text form (grammar.md principle 5), quote fidelity and locators, claim support and marking, screen vs narration, credits and source lines.
overall: The evidence work in ep03 is strong. I checked 14 of the 17 on-screen quotes against the local excerpt, the scratch transcripts (e27, p01, e35, ferriss), the 2011/2015/2016 GTD Times posts, the Weekly Review PDF, the Lonsdale snapshot and the Mabrey essay. Every one of them is verbatim, and almost every quote_zh is plain and faithful. Every number and date on screen matches its source, apart from the averaging word in b16. All cited claims are 'checked', and the series' own reading (b13 Lonsdale row, b21) is dashed and labelled. The one real error is the b18 'his claims' table. Its second quote is a fragment that leaves out 'your brain did not evolve to', so it states no claim, and the narration never mentions it. Next in priority come wording drift between narration and screen: b3 says the second edition renamed the steps while the screen shows the 2014 website; Clarify is glossed three ways; and b19 shows 全组 where the narration says 公司里人人. The rest are citation style (unidentifiable short refs in the b20 source line, ch. 1 vs 第 1 章) and a few labels that use a dangling 他 or are lifted from the narration. verification/screen-text-ep03.md does not exist (only ep00 and ep01 have inventories), so this review worked from scenes.js and rendered frames. Sheets: <scratchpad>/review/ep03/s1.png and s2.png, with full frames s1-*.png and s2-*.png in the same folder.

findings.element: gtd-evidence table, row 2: K.quote('gtd.four-things-claim') under 他的说法, with 研究出处 未给出
findings.problem: The 'his claim' row shows only the tail of Allen's sentence: “remember, remind, prioritize, or manage relationships with more than four things” / 记住、提醒、排序，或者管理四件以上事情之间的关系. The subject and the negation are missing, so the row reads as a list of activities, or even the opposite of what he said. The narration never introduces this claim. It enters while the voice says 在我读到的访谈和讲义里, so a viewer cannot tell what is being asserted.
findings.evidence: ferriss.txt line 98: “your head’s a crappy office… And your brain did not evolve to remember, remind, prioritize, or manage relationships with more than four things. That’s new cognitive science data, by the way.” Full frame s1-0296.900.png shows the fragment as the second 他的说法 row. scenes.js line 596 shows it at T('gtd.b18','将来')+0.3. b18 narration names only 脑子分不清过去和将来.
findings.fix: Have the main session widen the ledger quote to “your brain did not evolve to remember, remind, prioritize, or manage relationships with more than four things” and set quote_zh to 大脑没有进化到能记住、提醒、排序或管理四件以上事情之间的关系. Optionally change row 2's right cell to 称是认知科学新数据 · 未给出出处, since he did invoke research without citing any. Either add a clause to b18 (比如脑子分不清过去和将来、记不住四件以上的事), or drop row 2 and keep the table to what is narrated.

findings.element: 五个步骤的叫法 rows: 2001 · 目录章名 / 2014 · 官网五步
findings.problem: The narration says the 2015 second edition renamed the five steps (二〇一五年出了全面改写的第二版，书里讲的五个步骤也换了叫法). On screen, the new names are dated 2014 and attributed to the website, a year before the edition being described. The screen is the accurate side, because the 2015 text was never read. Still, a viewer hears 2015/书里 and sees 2014/官网 at the same moment.
findings.evidence: lab2 appears at T('gtd.b3','叫法')-0.4 ≈ 64.2 (scenes.js 158–164). gtd.wb2014-labels: the 2014-05-31 site archive already used Capture…Engage. gtd.version-split (inference) says the 2015 body text was not read at all. The only book-side support is the staff-relayed “subtle changes in the vocabulary” (staff-comment-vocabulary), which lists no step names.
findings.fix: Bring the narration in line with the evidence, e.g. 二〇一五年出了全面改写的第二版。五个步骤的叫法，官网二〇一四年就换了，Allen 说，原则一点没变. If the narration stays, relabel row 2 as 新叫法 · 官网 2014 起 so the screen at least does not appear to contradict it.

findings.element: GOAL2 每样输入事先拿定主意; 'Clarify 想清楚' (b7); '当场拿定主意 · Clarify' (b21)
findings.problem: The same step gets three different Chinese renderings on screen. b7 pairs Clarify with 想清楚, and b21 pairs it with 当场拿定主意. The 2001 goal it stands for reads 事先拿定主意 (b4, b7), so b21's 当场 contradicts that 事先. 当场 also echoes the two-minute rule's 当场做掉, which pulls Clarify toward that rule. Reflect is glossed 每周对一次账 in b21, while its chapter is 每周回顾. Principle 5 asks for the same wording wherever the same thing recurs.
findings.evidence: scenes.js line 175 (GOAL2), line 289 ('Clarify想清楚'), line 671 OUT = [['全收出来','Capture'…], ['当场拿定主意','Clarify'…], ['每周对一次账','Reflect'…]]. Frame s2-0343.400.png.
findings.fix: In b21, either reuse the established pairs (Capture 全收出来 · Clarify 想清楚 / 每样拿定主意 · Reflect 每周回顾) or drop the English step names from the reading boxes. Change 当场拿定主意 to 每样事先拿定主意, and make the b21 narration match (每一样事先拿定主意).

findings.element: K.source 'Ted Mabrey, Sorry, that isn’t an FDE, 2024 · Mabrey 2025 · Qureshi 2024'
findings.problem: Two of the three credits are bare surname-plus-year tags. No other source line in the episode uses that form, and a viewer cannot identify either work. The 'Mabrey 2025' credit carries ov.mabrey_impro_given_on_joining, a claim about Impro being handed to new hires. Its only bearing on this screen is the job title folded into its statement_zh. A fact-checker following the ID to verify 'Palantir 全球商务负责人' therefore lands on an unrelated claim.
findings.evidence: scenes.js lines 650–651. Ledger: ov.mabrey_impro_given_on_joining statement_zh begins 'Palantir 全球商务负责人 Ted Mabrey… 写：多年来 Palantir 员工入职时被给了 Impro'. The title actually comes from the sources.json author field ('title per palantir.com/partnerships/databricks').
findings.fix: Write the credits out in the episode's style: 'Ted Mabrey, Sorry, that isn’t an FDE, 2024 · Nabeel Qureshi, Reflections on Palantir, 2024'. Ask the main session for a dedicated checked claim for Mabrey's title (from the palantir.com page) and cite that, rather than the Impro claim.

findings.element: gtd-group-lab '最好的一面 · 全组看得到'
findings.problem: The label narrows the source, and it differs from the narration spoken over it. Saraf's 'best part' is seeing everything that happens at the company, and the narration says 让公司里的信息人人都看得到. The label says only the team (全组) can see.
findings.evidence: saraf.clean.txt line 58: “you could keep a running pulse of everything that happens at the company in real-time just by watching folders in your inbox”. Line 56: meeting reports went to a list 'often the entire company'. scenes.js line 623. Frame s2-0310.400.png.
findings.fix: Relabel as 最好的一面 · 全公司动态人人看得到, or the shorter 最好的一面 · 人人看得到, keeping it parallel with 另一面 · 每人收太多.

findings.element: Labels '他的说法' (b18 header), '中高层 · 他的辅导经验' / '典型专业人士 · 他的讲义' (b16), 'Joe Lonsdale · 写 Peter Thiel 的文章' (b13 kicker), '自己的那套系统' (b21)
findings.problem: Several structural labels carry the narration's voice. One uses a dangling pronoun (他), one is a clause cut from the narration (写 Peter Thiel 的文章), and one keeps a spoken demonstrative (那套). Grammar.md principle 5 rules out 悬空的指代 and narration excerpts in structural positions. The episode already names him in comparable labels (b11 'Allen 见过的待办清单'). 写 Peter Thiel 的文章 is also ambiguous between 'about Thiel' and 'by Thiel'.
findings.evidence: scenes.js lines 588, 534, 536, 453, 665. Narration b13: 'Joe Lonsdale 写 Peter Thiel 的那篇文章里提过这一条'. Narration b21: '自己的那套系统'.
findings.fix: Use 'Allen 的说法 | 研究出处'; 'Allen 的辅导经验' / 'Allen 的讲义'; 'Joe Lonsdale · Lessons from Peter Thiel · 一句提及' (the title stays in English, as the series rule allows); '自己的系统'.

findings.element: Kicker 'Getting Things Done · 2001 · 第 1 章开头', two quote locators 'David Allen, Getting Things Done, 2001, ch. 1', source line 'David Allen, Getting Things Done, 2001, 第 1 章'
findings.problem: One frame shows the same citation four times, in two locator styles (ch. 1 and 第 1 章). The style also varies elsewhere in the episode. The Lonsdale locator has no year, unlike every other locator. The b16 source line names 'The Three-fold Nature of Work' with no author or year. The b12 source line omits Ferriss #384, although gtd.two-min-spoken-2019 is among its claims.
findings.evidence: Full frame s1-0087.500.png. Ledger screen_locator 'Joe Lonsdale, Lessons from Peter Thiel, 8VC' (page meta 'Apr 11, 2010'). scenes.js lines 168–170, 196, 437–438, 549.
findings.fix: Use one locator form throughout, e.g. '…, 2001, 第 1 章' in both quotes and source lines. On b4, drop the kicker or hide the per-quote locators (o.locator=false) so the source line carries the citation once. Set the Lonsdale locator to '…, 8VC, 2010', write 'David Allen, The Three-fold Nature of Work, 2016', and add '· The Tim Ferriss Show #384, 2019' to the b12 line, or drop that claim ID.

findings.element: Lonsdale quote_zh '只要几分钟的任务，你不会往后拖' and the Lonsdale-row box '几分钟能做完', set under Allen's '两分钟内做完'
findings.problem: 'a couple minutes' is closer to 一两分钟 than to 几分钟. With the two rows aligned column by column, 两分钟 vs 几分钟 looks like a third difference, a loosened threshold. Neither the source nor the series' inference makes that claim: gtd.lonsdale-vs-author says the paraphrase agrees in substance and only drops the two conditions.
findings.evidence: Lonsdale snapshot, lesson 6: 'in GTD, you don’t put off tasks that only take a couple minutes'. Full frame s1-0222.000.png.
findings.fix: Render the quote as 只要一两分钟的任务，你不会往后拖, and the box as 一两分钟能做完. Optionally say 一两分钟 in the narration too.

findings.element: gtd-cost-val '每天约 1 小时'
findings.problem: The handout gives an average, which the narration renders correctly as 平均每天. The screen's 约 turns that average into 'approximately', a slightly different quantity.
findings.evidence: Threefold-Nature-of-Work.txt: 'requires an average of one hour per day, for the typical professional'. scenes.js line 538.
findings.fix: Change the label to 平均每天 1 小时.

findings.element: 第二版 card sub-line '全面改写'
findings.problem: 全面改写 appears as a plain property of the second edition. Its only support is publisher marketing copy, which AGENTS.md says must be marked apart from book text and the author's material. The source line marks 出版方文案 only as one of three sources lumped together.
findings.evidence: gtd.blurb-rewritten statement_zh: '这是营销文字，不是对书中改动的清单' (source kind publisher-marketing). scenes.js line 134.
findings.fix: Change the sub-line to 出版方称全面改写. Alternatively, cite the author's own 2019 remark (gtd.fer-tweaked-language: 更新不少、明显调整措辞) and label it as such.

findings.element: '德鲁克 · 管理学家' over '知识工作者的头号任务：界定自己的工作'
findings.problem: The line appears as Drucker's own position. The only evidence is Allen paraphrasing Drucker in a speech, and the ledger has no Drucker source. The narration frames it correctly (他引过…德鲁克的看法), but the screen drops the 'as cited by Allen' layer.
findings.evidence: e27.txt line 15: 'Peter Drucker… he would caution all of you as knowledge workers that your biggest task is defining what your work is'. Source line: David Allen, GTD Podcast #27, 2017.
findings.fix: Relabel the small heading as 'Allen 转述德鲁克' (or '德鲁克 · Allen 转述').

lens: Words on screen and their evidence: structural text (grammar.md principle 5), quote fidelity, claim support, screen vs narration, credits and source lines
overall: The evidence work holds up well. I checked every Dalio quote_en against the pdftotext of both copies, the 2016 106-page re-layout and the 2015 123-page public copy, and each one is verbatim in both apart from page-break hyphens and one comma that is a semicolon in the 2015 copy. The Chinese renderings of the Dalio quotes I spot-checked are faithful (#5, p.33, p.14 n15, p.31, p.32, #31, #31b, #195b, #24, #8, #15, #209, p.43, #34). Every claim on screen is checked, and the series' own readings are drawn dashed and labelled. The most serious problem is a credit: the line saying other former employees never described Palantir's use of the PDF shows only Qureshi's essay as its source, but it is this series' own search result. Next, the page numbers belong to the 2016 copy, while the credit text fits both copies, and the episode itself presents the 2015 copy as the one Qureshi could have got. After that, a handful of labels drop qualifiers the source states: "more or less", "though often much worse", "or lack of actions", "how well they manage". A few on-screen wordings also differ from what the narration says at the same moment. Note that verification/screen-text-ep04.md does not exist; the inventory in the scratchpad (inv.json) was made from the live stage.

findings.element: pr-scope dashed panel line "其他前员工的公开材料 · 未见描述" under source line "Nabeel Qureshi, Reflections on Palantir, 2024"
findings.problem: This is the series' own negative search result, but on screen it is credited only to Qureshi's essay. A viewer reads it as something Qureshi stated, and Qureshi says nothing about other former employees.
findings.evidence: scenes.js:238 passes K.source(root, NQ, …, ['pr.qureshi-silent','pr.no-firsthand-else']). Claim pr.no-firsthand-else is claim_type unresolved and review_state checked-with-limits. Its locators are the project's search log ('WebSearch x3, Exa search x5, HN Algolia x3 …'), and its limits read '检索限于公开网页…也没有联系任何人'. Its source_id is nonetheless pr:qureshi-reflections, so the error starts in the ledger.
findings.fix: Reword the line to "本系列检索的公开网页 · 未见描述". Change the source line to "Nabeel Qureshi, Reflections on Palantir, 2024 · 本系列检索，公开网页，2026-10". In the ledger, give pr.no-firsthand-else a source entry for the search log instead of pr:qureshi-reflections.

findings.element: kq-zh of ov.list_qureshi_principles_pdf: "我还拿到一份后来成为 Ray Dalio《Principles》的早期 PDF。这些定下了调子。" (highlighted span "这些定下了调子。")
findings.problem: The Chinese makes the singular "This set the tone." plural (这些). That settles an ambiguity the source leaves open: 这些 means the books plus the PDF. It also differs from the narration, which says "这定下了调子" at the moment the phrase lights up in blue. The 《》 around Principles also breaks the series rule that English titles stay plain.
findings.evidence: quote_en: 'I also got an early PDF version of what became Ray Dalio’s Principles. This set the tone.' (Qureshi snapshot line 161). Narration pr.b1: '紧接着他写了一句，这定下了调子', with 定 at 28.78 s. scenes.js:108–109 lights hlz '这些定下了调子。' at T('定下')−0.2.
findings.fix: In the ledger, set quote_zh to "我还拿到一份后来成为 Ray Dalio 的 Principles 的早期 PDF。这定下了调子。" and set hlz to '这定下了调子。'. ep04 is the only episode that displays this quote_zh.

findings.element: pr-count "回顾全文提到这份 PDF 1 处" vs pr-panel-li "Qureshi 的回顾 · 只此一句"
findings.problem: The same fact appears in two different wordings, against grammar.md principle 5 (same wording wherever it recurs). "只此一句" is also wrong: the mention is two sentences.
findings.evidence: Qureshi snapshot line 161 is the only PDF/Dalio mention: 'I also got an early PDF version … Principles. This set the tone.' That is two sentences. Narration pr.b1 says '提到这份 PDF 的就这么一处'. Claim pr.qureshi-silent says '只有上述一句'.
findings.fix: Change the panel line to "Qureshi 的回顾 · 只此一处". Change pr.qureshi-silent to '只有上述一处（两句）'.

findings.element: pr-role "Bridgewater 创始人 · 1975"; pr-mark-lab "2015 夏 · Qureshi 入职"
findings.problem: In two places a fact stays on screen without its credit. The 1975 credit fades about 0.5 s after "1975" appears, and the next line cites only the Internet Archive while 1975 stays up for another 4 s. The 2015-summer label carries Qureshi's claim ID, but its visible source line never names his essay.
findings.evidence: scenes.js:130 keeps the PDF source, claim pr.dalio-founded-1975, until T('这些原则')−0.1 ≈ 37.0 s. The role label appears at 36.2 s (创 at 36.37 s). The 40.0 s frame shows 1975 with only "Internet Archive · bwater.com 存档记录". In scenes.js:170 the line reads 'Internet Archive · bwater.com 存档记录 · Ray Dalio, Principles, PDF, © 2011' but carries pr.qureshi-joined-2015, whose source is pr:qureshi-reflections ('I joined in summer 2015').
findings.fix: pr-dalio: show one line, "Ray Dalio, Principles, PDF, © 2011 · Internet Archive · bwater.com 存档记录", from T(b2)+0.3 to the end of the scene, with all three claim IDs. pr-strip: append " · Nabeel Qureshi, Reflections on Palantir, 2024".

findings.element: Source and kq-loc lines "Ray Dalio, Principles, PDF, © 2011, p. 5 / p. 20 / pp. 17–18 / p. 33 / p. 14, note 15 / p. 24 / pp. 24, 41 / p. 31 / p. 32 / p. 43"; end-card entries "Principles by Ray Dalio (© 2011 text; PDF file created 2016-03-04)" and "Ray Dalio, Principles, PDF, © 2011"
findings.problem: The page numbers are those of the 2016 106-page re-layout. The credit text describes both copies equally, and at 42–70 s the episode presents the 2015 123-page copy as the one public when Qureshi joined. A fact-checker opening that copy lands on the wrong pages. The same credit text is also used for pr.dalio-founded-1975, which comes from the 2015 copy. The end card lists two Principles entries a viewer cannot tell apart.
findings.evidence: Page found by pdftotext, 2016 copy vs 2015 copy: 'not for you to blindly follow' p5 / p3; pr.fail-33 p33 / p31; pr.pain-bounded p14 / p10; pr.machine-loop p24 / p22; pr.feedback-41 p41 / p39; pr.tested-40-years p43 / p41 (its own locator says 'p. 43 of the 106-page copy'); pr.pain-reflect p20 / p17. Every page of both copies is footed '© 2011 Ray Dalio'. Source pr:dalio-2011-pdf has no credit_zh, so its raw title appears on the end card.
findings.fix: Name the copy in each screen_locator, e.g. "Ray Dalio, Principles, PDF © 2011, 2016 重排版, p. 31". Alternatively, switch to 2015-copy page numbers, since that is the copy the episode puts forward. Give the two sources distinct credit_zh: "… 2015 公开版，123 页" and "… 2016 重排版，106 页".

findings.element: source line "Principles PDF，© 2011，2015 年公开版与 2016 年重排版比对 · Internet Archive"; badge "0.936 按词比对 序列相似度"
findings.problem: 0.936 is the series' own measurement, but the credit reads as though the Internet Archive did the comparison. The line's style also differs from every other Principles credit: full-width commas and no author. In the ledger, a claim cited on this same line still says the texts were never compared.
findings.evidence: pr.version-2015-match gives the locator 'word-level diff, main session 2026-10-17'. The narration ('我…逐词对了一遍') makes the comparison first-person; the credit does not. pr.ver-2015-public, cited on the same line, has the limit '这份与本地文件的正文是否逐字相同未比对', which contradicts version-2015-match.
findings.fix: Use the source line "本系列比对 · Ray Dalio, Principles, PDF, © 2011 · 2015 公开版（Internet Archive 2015-08 存档）与 2016 重排版". Update the limit on pr.ver-2015-public to point to pr.version-2015-match.

findings.element: pr-flat-lab "其余所有人 · 同一头衔" and "五六位总监与 CEO"
findings.problem: The label drops Qureshi's qualifier "more or less" and states uniform titles as fact. Meanwhile the narration says 差不多 at that moment, so screen and narration disagree in evidence strength. The narration also says "几位总监和首席执行官" where the screen says "五六位" and "CEO".
findings.evidence: Qureshi snapshot line 175: 'everyone had the “forward deployed engineer” title, more or less, and apart from that there were five or six Directors and the CEO.' Narration pr.b22 has '总监' at 300.7 s and '头衔都差不多' at 302.8 s.
findings.fix: Change the label to "其余所有人 · 大致同一头衔". Change the narration to "除了五六位总监和 CEO" so names and numbers match the screen.

findings.element: pr-col-t "Dalio · Bridgewater" beside "Qureshi 记得的 Palantir"
findings.problem: The two column titles are not parallel, and the same subject is called "Dalio 笔下的 Bridgewater" throughout 制度. The short form also loses the marker that the left column is Dalio's written account, the counterpart of Qureshi's memory on the right. That keeps book text and eyewitness apart.
findings.evidence: scenes.js:10 defines BW = 'Dalio 笔下的 Bridgewater', used as the label at 231.5–277 s. scenes.js:646 writes 'Dalio · Bridgewater'. The quote is normative ('We have, and should have…', #34).
findings.fix: Use "Dalio 笔下的 Bridgewater" for the left column title.

findings.element: grid headers "反复做成过 / 没有做成过", "讲得清道理 / 讲不清道理"; pr-novice "没经验的人 · 有时有极好的想法"
findings.problem: The 可信度 labels shift Dalio's terms. Lacking "repeatedly and successfully accomplished" is labelled 没有做成过, which means never done it. The novice line keeps only the upside and drops his counterweight. The narration differs from the screen: 排在其次 vs 有些可信, and 很好 vs 极好.
findings.evidence: #31b (2016 p60): 'People who have repeatedly and successfully accomplished the thing in question … Those with one of those two qualities are somewhat believable' and 'inexperienced people can have great ideas, sometimes far better than more experienced people, though often much worse.' Narration says '排在其次' at 200.6 s and '没经验的人，有时也会有很好的想法' at 208.4 s.
findings.fix: Change the column header to "没有反复做成过". Change the novice line to "没经验的人 · 想法有时远胜老手，也常常差得多". Align the narration to "有些可信" and to the same novice wording.

findings.element: pr-kind "一个动作 · 用动词描述" (beside its example "“我没查时刻表”") and "人的特点 · 用形容词描述"
findings.problem: The label calls a proximate cause an action, but the example shown next to it is a non-action. Dalio's definition explicitly covers both. The label also drops "typically" from both rows.
findings.evidence: 2016 p32: 'Proximate causes typically are the actions or lack of actions that lead to problems … typically described via verbs … Root causes are typically described with adjectives'. pr.diag-root statement_zh: '导致问题的行动或不作为'.
findings.fix: Change the labels to "动作或不作为 · 通常用动词描述" and "人的特点 · 通常用形容词描述".

findings.element: pr-card "我因为累了工作表现差" (and "睡不够")
findings.problem: The example on screen differs from the one spoken at the same moment. The card's wording comes from the ledger's paraphrase, not from a rendering checked against the source. In the next segment the examples are in quotation marks, but these cards are not.
findings.evidence: scenes.js:381 takes the card text from said('pr.diag-31', /如“([^”]+)”/), i.e. statement_zh. Narration pr.b11 says '我因为太累，工作做得不好' with 太 at 155.5 s, and the card appears at 155.2 s. Source p31: '“I am performing badly in my job because I am tired.”'
findings.fix: Make the card read "“我因为太累，工作做得不好”" and put "睡不够" in quotation marks too, so it matches the b12 examples.

findings.element: pr-loop "反馈回路" + "好组织与坏组织 · 最大的差别所在"
findings.problem: The shortened label says the loop itself is the biggest difference. The source, and the narration at that moment, put the difference in how well the loop is managed. That is a qualifier lost in condensing (grammar.md principle 5).
findings.evidence: pr.feedback-41: 'the most important difference between great organizations and bad ones is in how well they manage their feedback loops.' Narration pr.b10: '最大的差别就在反馈回路管得好不好', with 好组织 at 139.7 s.
findings.fix: Change the label to "反馈回路管得好坏 · 好组织与坏组织的最大差别".

findings.element: kq-zh "批评似乎很受容忍，也很受欢迎" vs narration
findings.problem: The screen keeps Qureshi's hedge "it seemed". The narration drops it and adds an escalation, so speech states more than the quote shown under it.
findings.evidence: Snapshot line 159: 'it seemed that criticism was highly tolerated and welcomed'. Narration pr.b23 at 308.7 s: 'Palantir 很容得下批评，甚至欢迎批评'.
findings.fix: Change the narration to "Qureshi 写过，在 Palantir，批评看起来很受容忍，也很受欢迎。"

findings.element: pr-both "本集引文 · 两份都有"
findings.problem: The label is broader than the claim. The episode also quotes Qureshi and The New Yorker, and neither appears in either PDF.
findings.evidence: pr.version-2015-match: '本集引用的原则编号与原话在两份中都有'. Only Dalio's text was compared.
findings.fix: Change it to "本集所引 Dalio 原文 · 两份都有".

findings.element: 《Principles》 in kq-zh; "Dalio 的原则" in the pr.ny-dispute kq-zh; "Copeland 的 The Fund · 据《纽约客》"; end-card entries "Open Library record for ISBN 9781501124020 (…)", "Internet Archive, bwater.com captures", "A Hedge-Fund Founder's Obsessive Storytelling (Tarpley Hitt, The New Yorker)"
findings.problem: Titles are rendered inconsistently across the episode. Principles appears plain, in 《》, and translated as 原则. The New Yorker appears both as 《纽约客》 and in English in the same scene. The end card shows raw English ledger titles where the body uses "Internet Archive · bwater.com 存档记录" and author-first credits.
findings.evidence: Ledger-patch quote_zh for pr.ny-dispute renders 'Dalio’s Principles' as 'Dalio 的原则'. The source line at 286–292 s reads 'Tarpley Hitt, The New Yorker, 2023-11-16'. Sources main:openlibrary-principles-2017, pr:newyorker-hitt-2023 and pr:ia-cdx have no credit_zh.
findings.fix: Keep Principles in English in both quote_zh: "Dalio 的 Principles" and no 《》. Write "据 The New Yorker". Add credit_zh to those three sources in the body's style, e.g. "Internet Archive · bwater.com 存档记录", "Tarpley Hitt, The New Yorker, 2023-11-16", "Open Library · Principles: Life and Work, 2017".

findings.element: pr-bar "bwater.com 公开版 · 123 页" with endpoints "2012-01" and "2016-03"
findings.problem: The endpoints are the first and last archive captures of that file. The bar reads as the dates the file was served.
findings.evidence: pr.ver-2015-public: digest unchanged across captures from 2012-01-10 to 2016-03-04. Per sources.json the PDF was created 2011-09-28, and the CDX query started at 2011-02-21.
findings.fix: Add a small qualifier to the endpoints, e.g. "存档所见 2012-01 — 2016-03".

lens: The picture as a viewer experiences it with the narration: sync, pacing, layout and legibility, visual grammar, images
overall: Sync is the episode's strength. Almost every element lands within about 0.3 s of its anchor word, the chapter changes cross-fade with no paper-only gap over about 1 s, nothing overflows the 80 px margins, and the David Allen photo is readable, credited and on topic. The mail-flood motif and its b19 callback work well, and red is used only for breakage. The most serious problem is the b3 edition timeline. It puts the author's later material (podcasts and interviews from 2011 to 2020, mostly after 2015) on a time axis between 2001 and 2015, which misstates the chronology of the evidence. Next, the b18 evidence table: the screen does not change for about 6.5 s while the narration makes its key point (no independent evaluation exists), and its second row is a quote the narration never mentions. The rest is grammar drift. Dashed lines also mean "not read" or "not written", not only the series' reading. Blue from an earlier beat stays on screen, so a later point of the moment competes with several blues or loses to them. (No verification/screen-text-ep03.md exists, so the stage was the only reference.)

findings.element: gtd-editions timeline: '2001 第一版' / '作者后来的说法 (官网 · 讲义 · 访谈)' / '2015 第二版 未读'
findings.problem: The middle card sits on the year axis between the 2001 and 2015 dots. That tells the viewer the author's later statements came before the second edition. In fact, nearly all the 'later statements' the episode quotes come after 2015. The narration's '之后的内容' means the rest of the book's content, not a period of time; the drawing reads it as a time span.
findings.evidence: Full frame at 62.4 s: the dot for '作者后来的说法' is at x≈960 on the line from 2001 (x≈440) to 2015 (x≈1480). Sources quoted later in this episode: GTD Times 2011 and 2015, Podcast #1 2015, #17 2016, #27 2017, #35 2017, Tim Ferriss #384 2019, Podcast #79 2020, gettingthingsdone.com (2014 archive and current site). Script b3: '只到第一章开头；之后的内容，用的是他在官网、讲义和访谈里的说法'.
findings.fix: Keep the axis for the two editions only. Take the middle card off the axis: either a separate row under it labelled '其余内容 · 作者 2011–2020 的说法', or place it after the 2015 dot with a '2011–2020' year span. Give it no axis dot.

findings.element: gtd-evidence table (他的说法 / 研究出处 / 第二版 · 加进认知研究 未读)
findings.problem: The last change ('未读' fades in) lands at about 292.1 s. The screen then holds unchanged for about 6.5 s, while the narration moves to a new and central point: there is no independent research or evaluation of whether the method works. Nothing on screen marks it.
findings.evidence: Frames 292.4, 295.2, 297.0 and 298.5 are identical. Timeline: '管不管用' 293.83, '独立' 295.62, '评估' 296.57, end of b18 297.08; the scene runs to b19+0.2 = 299.0.
findings.fix: Add a final row at T('gtd.b18','独立') − 0.2, for example '方法效果 · 独立研究或评估' in the left column and '未找到' in the right column, styled like the '未给出' cells. A light 'one plain limit' phrase is enough.

findings.element: Second row quote gtd.four-things-claim: “remember, remind, prioritize, or manage relationships with more than four things” / 记住、提醒、排序，或者管理四件以上事情之间的关系
findings.problem: The narration gives only one example ('比如脑子分不清过去和将来') and never mentions this claim. The quote is a fragment with no subject and no predicate, so it reads as a list of verbs, not a statement. A viewer can't tell what Allen claimed or why it sits under '研究出处 未给出'.
findings.evidence: Full frame at 295.2 s: the row shows only the fragment and its locator. The claim's statement_zh says the brain has not evolved to hold more than four things, and that Allen called this new cognitive-science data. That predicate appears nowhere on screen. Script b18 never mentions four things.
findings.fix: Either drop the row, or give it a short label above the quote that carries the claim, such as '大脑同时顾不过四件以上的事' (written as a structural noun phrase, per grammar rule 5), shown at T('gtd.b18','那些道理') so the plural '那些道理' points to it.

findings.element: Allen row in the Allen-vs-Lonsdale comparison: '两分钟内做完' greyed, '当场做掉' filled blue
findings.problem: The '两分钟内做完' box was greyed at 205.4 s to mean 'not a hard rule'. That quote is hidden at 208.7 s, but the grey state carries into the comparison. There, grey text in a pale box looks like the dashed '未提' boxes, so it reads as if Allen's rule lacks the time limit while Lonsdale's line has it in solid ink. At '两个前提', the filled blue '当场做掉' is also the heaviest element on screen and competes with the two outlined blue premises, which are the actual point.
findings.evidence: Full frame at 221.2 s: Allen row, '两分钟内做完' in grey on a pale border directly above Lonsdale's solid black '几分钟能做完'; '当场做掉' a solid blue block; '下一步已定' and '本来就要做' only blue-outlined. Anchors: 更费时 205.62, 写 209.56, 两个前提 220.71.
findings.fix: At lonsAt − 0.8 (when the row moves down), return A.boxes[3] to ink. Switch A.boxes[4] to the 'end plain' style used in Lonsdale's row, so the two premises are the only blue at 220.5 s.

findings.element: Dashed '第二版 · 全面改写 · 未读' card and dot; dashed tag '处理方式 · 未写明'; dashed box '第二版 · 加进认知研究 · 未读'
findings.problem: Dashed lines mean three things in this episode: not read (b3, b18), not written in the email (b7), and the series' own reading (b13 legend, b21). The b13 legend explicitly teaches '----- 原文未提 · 本系列的读法'. A viewer who has learned that will take the dashed second-edition boxes as the series' inference. The b7 tag describes something Allen says, so by the series' rules it should be solid.
findings.evidence: scenes.css header: 'Dashed: not read, not stated by the source, or this series' reading'. Classes .gtd-ed-card.dash, .gtd-ed-dot.dash, .gtd-env-tag and .gtd-ed2 all use dashed borders, and none carries the '本系列的读法' label. The b13 legend appears at 220.6 s and the b21 legend at 324.9 s.
findings.fix: Keep dashed lines for the b13 comparison and b21 only. Draw unread or absent items in one other consistent way, for example a solid hairline in --rule with grey text and an explicit '未读' tag. Make the b7 '处理方式 · 未写明' tag a solid box, or plain grey text.

findings.element: Weekly-review screen (回顾 chips, '一到两小时', quote rule, five '下一步' tags); field screen label '最好的一面 · 全组看得到'
findings.problem: Blue from earlier beats is never released. At 238.9 s there are about 13 blue elements: six week chips, the cadence, the quote rule and five '下一步' tags. The point of the moment, every project having a next action, does not stand out. In b19 the opposite happens: when the narration turns to '另一面', the lines go grey, but the earlier label stays blue and the new point '另一面 · 每人收太多' is in ink. The emphasis is reversed.
findings.evidence: Full frame at 238.9 s. Full frame at 309.6 s: the left label is blue and the right label black while the narrator says '每个人收进来的东西都太多' (308.94).
findings.fix: b14: at T('gtd.b14','项目') − 0.3, take the six 回顾 chips and the '一到两小时' text back to ink, leaving only the '下一步' tags blue. b19: at T('gtd.b19','另一面') − 0.3, take the 'see' label to ink, and either make 'much' the accent or leave both in ink. Consider centring a single label, because the left/right halves meant two groups of people in b1.

findings.element: Cost chart: '头一回全收出来 1–6 小时' and '处理新进来的东西 每天约 1 小时' on one hour axis
findings.problem: A one-off total and a per-day rate share one axis. The daily hour looks like the small cost next to a big 1–6 h bar, while the narration's '平均每天就得花一个小时' stresses that it adds up.
findings.evidence: Full frame at 260.9 s: the blue 0–1 bar sits under a 1–6 bar on the same 0–6 '小时' scale.
findings.fix: Give the daily row its own unit: draw it as a strip of repeated one-hour blocks under '每天' labels, or move it to its own small scale labelled '每天'. Don't put the two rows on one shared axis.

findings.element: Chapter tag at top left
findings.problem: For 23 s the tag reads '两个目标' over the editions and step-names content, before the two goals appear at b4. During the time-cost scene it reads '每周回顾', though that scene matches the next chapter, '作者讲的代价'.
findings.evidence: script.json chapters: '两个目标' at gtd.b3, '作者讲的代价' at gtd.b17. Frames at 62.4 s and 260.9 s.
findings.fix: In script.json (main session), start '两个目标' at gtd.b4 and give b3 its own short chapter (for example '版本与出处'). Start '作者讲的代价' at gtd.b16.

findings.element: Checklist rows '收件处清零 / 各张清单过一遍 / 项目逐个看过'
findings.problem: The narration lists three checks. The first two get ticked on their words, but '项目逐个看过' stays empty even as the narration says '一个个项目看过去', so the list stops responding halfway.
findings.evidence: Ticks happen at 233.75 and 234.96 only. Full frame at 238.9 s shows the third box empty.
findings.fix: Tick rows[2] at T('gtd.b14','项目') − 0.2, at the same time the project panel appears.

lens: Picture as a viewer experiences it with the narration: sync, pacing and holds, layout and legibility, visual grammar, images
overall: The picture mostly tracks the narration closely. I resolved every word anchor in scenes.js against the per-character timings, and almost all land 0.1–0.3 s before the word. Layouts are clean: all text is 30 px or larger, the 80 px margins hold, nothing overlaps or gets clipped, every quote and source line carries a claim, and the one photograph is credited on screen. The weak spots are in a few places. In b10 the payoff "反馈回路" and the blue loop appear about 3 s before the narrator says it. The tail of b7 holds a single unhighlighted quote for 9 s while the only blue on screen is a stale "Reflection". The body ends with a one-frame cut to blank paper before the outro. In b3 the blue builds up on old items instead of moving to the current point. For a fact-checker, every Principles page locator ("PDF, © 2011, p. N") uses the 2016 106-page re-layout, while the episode presents the 123-page 2015 copy, so the page numbers don't match that copy. Dashed lines in b3–b4 mean "unknown" with no 本系列的读法 label, which muddies the dashed/solid grammar the episode sets up later.

findings.element: pr-machine: .pr-loop '反馈回路' + '好组织与坏组织 · 最大的差别所在', loop arrows turning blue
findings.problem: The answer arrives about 3 s before the narrator gives it, and the label order is the reverse of the sentence. The loop turns blue and the big blue '反馈回路' shows while the voice is still on '他认为好组织跟坏组织…'. The word 反馈回路 is only reached at the end of the 4.9 s segment.
findings.evidence: T('pr.b10','反馈回路') = 142.32. The loop stroke goes BLUE at T('pr.b10')-0.1 = 138.91 (scenes.js:367-369). name.children are shown at T('pr.b10','好组织')-0.25 = 139.42 with stagger 0.5, so the bold '反馈回路' (first child) comes first and the subtitle second (scenes.js:372-374). Frame 139.0 already shows the blue loop. Frame 140.5 shows '反馈回路' fully up while the narration is at '坏组织' (140.42).
findings.fix: Show the subtitle first, then the term on its word. K.show(name.lastChild, T('pr.b10','好组织')-0.25); K.show(name.firstChild, T('pr.b10','反馈回路')-0.2); and move the tl.to(loop,{stroke:BLUE}) to T('pr.b10','反馈回路')-0.3. Fading cmp/design/people at b10 can stay where it is.

findings.element: pr-pain: quote pr.fail-33 (and header formula with 'Reflection' lit blue)
findings.problem: For 9 s nothing changes while the narration moves through three new points: others won't point out mistakes, so there is no objective diagnosis, so growth is stunted. The only blue on screen is 'Reflection' in the header, lit at 103.7 for '看清'. It no longer marks the point of the moment.
findings.evidence: q.root for pr.fail-33 is shown at T('pr.b7','多数人')-0.2 = 110.57 with no hl/hlz (scenes.js:308-309). There are no further tweens until pr-dose fades in at 119.67. Frames 111.2, 115.0 and 119.0 are identical. Narration anchors: 指出来 113.75, 诊断 116.67, 受了阻 118.6. AUTHORING asks for a matching step inside any segment longer than 4 s.
findings.fix: Pass highlights and step through them. hl: ['reluctant to point out mistakes in others', 'an objective diagnosis of problems arising from people’s mistakes is often missing', 'personal evolution is stunted'], hlz: ['不愿指出别人的错误', '缺少客观的诊断', '个人的进化也受到阻碍'] (all are substrings of the ledger text). lit/unlit them at 多数人, 诊断 and 受了阻. unlit(parts[2]) (Reflection) at T('pr.b7','多数人')-0.2, and dim the self/wall diagram there.

findings.element: pr-reading → pr-outro transition
findings.problem: The closing '本系列的读法' card vanishes in a single frame, chapter tag included. About 0.63 s of empty paper follows, then the outro fades in. It reads as a blink at the emotional close of the body.
findings.evidence: pr-reading runs to u.bodyEnd + 0.4 = 332.249 with no fade-out. pr-outro starts at T('pr.o1')-0.3 = 332.876 and fades in over 0.4 s (scenes.js:701, 719-723). Frame 332.24 shows the full card. Frames 332.26 and 332.6 are blank paper. Frame 332.9 shows the outro map at low opacity.
findings.fix: pr-outro is standalone-only, so start it so it overlaps the reading card, e.g. Film.scene('pr-outro', u.bodyEnd + 0.05, …) with its 0.4 s fade-in. That keeps pr-reading within bodyEnd+0.4 for the compilation. Alternatively add tl.to(root,{opacity:0,duration:0.3}, u.bodyEnd+0.1) to pr-reading so it never snaps.

findings.element: Source lines and quote locators 'Ray Dalio, Principles, PDF, © 2011, p. N'
findings.problem: The page numbers come from the 2016 re-laid-out 106-page file. The episode presents the 123-page 2015 bwater.com copy as the one in question, and both files say © 2011. A fact-checker who opens the 2015 copy named on screen and in the credits at the cited page won't find the quote.
findings.evidence: pdftotext of vault/snapshots/local/palantir-20261006/principles-dalio-2011.pdf (the 2016 file) puts 'not for you to blindly follow' on p5, 'too much pain can break' on p14, 'reluctant to point out mistakes' on p33 and 'tested over the last 40 years' on p43, matching the screen. The 2015 public text layer (vault/snapshots/local/palantir-series-20261017/dalio-principles-bwater-2015-public.txt) has them on p3, p10, p31 and p41. pr-strip and pr-compare tie '© 2011 · 123 页' to the 2015 copy. The end card lists both PDFs.
findings.fix: Name the layout in every locator. Set the PDF constant in scenes.js and the screen_locator fields in claims.jsonl to something like 'Ray Dalio, Principles, PDF © 2011（2016 重排版，106 页）, p. 20' (main session owns the ledger). Alternatively cite principle numbers (#8, #31…) only, since those match across both copies.

findings.element: pr-compare: blue on .pr-stamp, .pr-badge 0.936, #195b bars/tags/link, .pr-both, then .pr-sheet-lab
findings.problem: Blue piles up instead of marking the point of the moment. When the narration reaches the open question ('Qureshi 拿到的是不是这一份，没法确定'), the current item is grey while four earlier items are still blue. At '这里不用' both file labels turn blue as well, giving six-plus blue elements on one screen.
findings.evidence: Frame 64.4: stamp, 0.936, both #195b lines and tags, and '本集引文 · 两份都有' are all blue; '是否同一份 · 无法确定' is grey (.pr-open-lab ink3). Frame 69.6 adds both '2015 公开版 · 123 页' and '2016 重排版 · 106 页' in blue (scenes.js:216). None of the earlier items is ever unlit.
findings.fix: Move the accent along with the narration. Return the stamp to ink at T('pr.b3','换过'), the 0.936 number to ink at T('pr.b3','每一句'), and the #195b link, tags and '两份都有' to ink/grey at T('pr.b3','拿到')-0.3. Then only the labels are blue at '不用'.

findings.element: pr-compare dashed box 'Qureshi 拿到的早期 PDF' + dashed link; pr-scope dashed panel 'Palantir 的用法' (.pr-panel.open)
findings.problem: Here dashed is used to mean 'unknown / not found', with no '本系列的读法' label. Later in the episode (b22, b24) dashed is explicitly labelled 本系列的读法. On pr-compare the same screen draws the word-by-word comparison, itself the series' own measurement, in solid lines next to the dashed link. So the dashed/solid code carries two meanings.
findings.evidence: scenes.js:208-209 ('ln dash soft'), scenes.css:56 (.pr-open dashed), :64 (.pr-panel.open dashed). Frames 64.4 and 73.5 show the dashed elements with no legend. Frames 293.5 and 323.0 show the dashed legend '本系列的读法'. AUTHORING: dashed for the series' own inference, labelled '本系列的读法'; the same screen does not mix meanings.
findings.fix: Both statements are the narrator's own judgment ('没法确定', '我在公开材料里没找到'), so add the small dashed .pr-legend '本系列的读法' to these two scenes. If they are meant as a different category (open question), use a non-dashed treatment such as grey text, with no dashed border or link, so that dashed keeps a single meaning.

findings.element: pr-dalio portrait (asset pr.dalio-grameen-2017)
findings.problem: The photo is a blended video frame. At 600×760 px as the scene's main subject, the raised hand is see-through over the jacket, and ghost mic heads and stems float over the suit.
findings.evidence: Full-resolution frame 36.6, crop x 200–700 / y 450–950, shows the double exposure. assets.jsonl notes 'Video still, not a camera original.'
findings.fix: Frame tighter on head and shoulders (e.g. a 600×600 box with pos '50% 10%' that cuts the hand), or pick a cleaner frame or another licensed photo.

findings.element: pr-dose zones: '过多痛苦 / 把人压垮' (red) vs '没有痛苦 / 妨碍成长' (grey)
findings.problem: The claim, and the quote on the same screen, treat both extremes as failures. Only the too-much end is red, which suggests no pain is neutral.
findings.evidence: scenes.css:84-90 (.pr-zone.none paper3; .pr-zone.over red-soft; .pr-zone-bot.over red). pr.pain-bounded: 'too much pain can break someone and that the absence of pain typically prevents growth'. Frame 124.2.
findings.fix: Give both outer zones the same treatment, either both grey with blue only on 适度 or both red-soft, so the drawing matches the symmetric claim.

findings.element: pr-believe quote pr.bel-31 highlights
findings.problem: The three phrases the narration walks through (probability of being right, quality of reasoning, track record) are lit only in the English line. The Chinese translation, which most viewers will follow, stays flat. Every other highlighted quote in the episode lights both lines.
findings.evidence: scenes.js:460-465 passes hl only, no hlz. Frames 185.5, 189.8 and 192.0 show blue only in the English line.
findings.fix: Add hlz: ['一个人的看法正确的概率', '一个人推理的质量', '他过往的记录'] (substrings of quote_zh) and lit/unlit them together with q.hl.
